newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call flat, gilt yields recover after fall.
newsitem.headline: Indian call flat, gilt yields recover after fall.

text.p: Call money ended unchanged in the 5.25-5.75 percent range on Thursday amid comfortable liquidity and the absence of fresh market-moving factors, dealers said.

"Call rates have become highly predictable these days," a dealer at a foreign bank said. "Whenever lenders try to push up rates, there is resistance from borrowers and the market slips back into a narrow range."
Yields on government securities fell initially on buying interest from banks and corporates but recovered by the end of the day to Wednesday's closing levels, dealers said.

The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock was traded on Thursday at 13.04 percent against Wednesday's 13.03 percent while the 13.50 percent 1998 stock fell to 13.49 percent from 13.51 percent, dealers said.

Dealers said three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were quoted at 14 percent and three-month CDs at 11 percent. "But there is a difference of at least 25 basis points between buyer and seller quotes," a dealer said. "Few deals are being struck."
Three-month commercial paper was quoted 13.50 percent while inter-corporate deposits remained steady at 17.0-19.0 percent for top-rated borrowers.
